chitchat: "Everything Kesh puts in you, I made. Remember that when she takes the credit."
"A body's just a machine that whines about it. Mine stopped whining years ago."
description: A broad man whose arms are more chrome than the rest of him, in a scarred fab apron over a heat-stained shirt. He talks to you the way he talks to the machines: plainly, and only when there's a point.

bye.text: He grunts and turns back to the line.

line.text:
"This is the Weave. We spin the muscle, print the plate, blank the oculars — everything that goes into you starts as raw stock on my floor. Kesh just screws it in."

A flat look.

"When the clinic cannot get you a part, come to the source. Me."

options.label: Got anything that needs breaking in?

root.text: Duc doesn't look up from the gantry. "If you're lost, the Spire's back up the plaza. If you're not lost"—now he looks—"tell me what you need built."

tolerance_accept.text: "Kesh will fit it. Then go and do something stupid with it, and come back here so I can listen to it."

tolerance_carry.text:
"Load, then. That is the boring failure and the one I care about."

He puts the set on the bench and pushes it across with two fingers.

"Do not favour it. People favour a new one and then I get a clean part back and learn nothing."

tolerance_hit.text:
"Shock loading." Something that is nearly approval. "Good. That is where they break and nobody will admit to it on a form."

He puts the set on the bench and pushes it across with two fingers.

"Break it if it is going to break. I would rather find out on you than on a surgeon's table in nine years."

tolerance_offer.text:
"You have got a pulse and a poor sense of self-preservation. That is the whole specification." Duc wipes his hands on the apron and does not look up.

"Hand actuator. Second knuckle, index and middle — the two that do the gripping. Mine are good for eleven years and I want to know why the last batch came back at nine."

"I need it run in. Not tested. Tested is a bench and a week and it tells you nothing about what a hand actually does. Run in means out there, on somebody, doing work."

"So: what do you do with your hands all day?"

tolerance_report.text:
He puts a hand flat on your chest and goes very still, listening to something inside you that you cannot hear.

"Mm." A grunt that could mean anything. "Good numbers. You can go."

tolerance_return.text:
"One thing." He holds up a finger, and it is chrome to the second joint.

"The actuator comes back. Whatever else happens, the part comes back to this bench. If you are dead I will send somebody for it, and that is not a threat, it is a work order."

clothing_layers: a scarred fabrication apron over chrome-laced arms
steel-toed boots worn to the metal

name: Foreman Duc
